newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson has strong second quarter. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson has strong second quarter. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp. on Tuesday reported stronger second-quarter earnings, with strength in all three of its major divisions.
Dayton Hudson said it earned $130 million, or 54 cents a share, during the second quarter ended Aug. 2, vs $101 million, or 42 cents a share, during the same period a year ago.
This year's results included an $11 million, or 5-cent-a-share, charge for the redemption of debt. Minus the charge, Dayton Hudson earned 59 cents a share.
Wall Street analysts on average had expected the company to earn 55 cents a share, according to research firm First Call.
Revenues rose to $6.3 billion from $5.7 billion a year earlier.

"We are pleased with our overall financial performance in the second quarter and year to date," Dayton Hudson Chairman Bob Ulrich said in a statement. "All three divisions continued to contribute to our improvement in earnings in the second quarter."

The Target division's pretax profit rose 14 percent to $274 million. Target's total revenues increased 14 percent and same-store revenues -- revenues from stores open at least a year -- were up 6 percent. The gross margin rate fell due to higher markdowns, and the operating expense rate was flat compared with last year.

The Mervyn division's pretax profit was up 4 percent in the second quarter to $58 million. Revenues fell (corrects from rose) 5 percent, primarily reflecting closed stores, while comparable-store revenues increased 2 percent. Mervyn's gross margin rate fell due to higher markdowns, while the operating expense rate improved due to lower store expenses and headquarters costs.

At the Department Store Division, pretax profit was $33 million vs. $12 million in 1996. Total revenues rose 1 percent, and comparable-store revenues fell 1 percent. The division's gross margin rate increased, partially due to higher markup, and the operating expense rate improved significantly due to reductions in store expense and lower marketing costs.
Dayton Hudston stock was down 44 cents at $60.25 in late morning consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
